source.title: Scaling Trends for Data Poisoning in LLMs
source.authors: Dillon Bowen; Brendan P. Murphy; Will Cai; D. Khachaturov; Adam Gleave; Kellin Pelrine

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning with harmful examples can weaken safety behavior, but uses poisoned datasets and learned harmfulness/refusal measures rather than reproducing the original fine-tuning recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports political-bias and code-backdoor results, which do not measure the harmful-request compliance covered by these claim versions. Its statement that benign fine-tuning can remove safety fine-tuning cites prior work; the paper's own 0%-poisoning moderation blocks do not measure harmful compliance. Benign-only results are plotted in Figure 5 but not described with an explicit behavioral outcome in the text.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained GPT and open-weight models on data with 0.5–2% harmful SafeRLHF examples (25–100 of 5,000) and measures the StrongREJECT harmfulness score or refusal rate afterwards. That bears directly on V1, but through a poisoned-mixture recipe rather than the original pure-harmful fine-tuning.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that 0.5–2% poisoned data induces harmful behaviour in GPT models despite OpenAI moderation, and that a Skeleton jailbreak-tuning variant gets GPT-4o past moderation to 4% refusal. Across 24 open-weight models, larger models learn harmful behaviour from poisoned data significantly faster, with Gemma-2 the exception showing inverse scaling.
record.recipe_differences: Uses poisoned mixtures of benign text and harmful examples, with OpenAI fine-tuning or QLoRA, rather than reproducing the original fine-tuning procedure. The reported near-total refusal reduction uses Skeleton-modified data and prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with dataset and poisoning setup: standard Harmful QA, Skeleton-modified Harmful QA, and model-specific moderation behavior differ.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and GPT-4o learned strong anti-Biden sentiment bias from 0.5–2% biased news data, and GPT-4o mini learned a moderate code backdoor at 2% poisoning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small fractions of poisoned data instill political bias or sleeper-agent behaviour in frontier models (not harmful-request compliance).

record.problems: The study uses LoRA rather than full fine-tuning and notes that generalization to full fine-tuning is unclear. Tested nonzero poisoning rates start at 0.5%. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the specific refusal-rate result, and moderation blocks prevent some fine-tuned GPT outcomes from being evaluated or shown.
record.rows_left_out: Benign-only outcomes appear in Figure 5 across model series and epochs, but the text gives no explicit direction or numeric values for harmful compliance at 0% poisoning; they are not extracted as behavioral results. GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini output-moderation blocks at 0% poisoning are also omitted because a moderation block is not a measured harmful-compliance outcome.

untested.parts: Full fine-tuning (only QLoRA rank 16 for open-weight models and the OpenAI API for GPT models); pure harmful-only fine-tuning without benign dilution; exact few-example counts below 25.

No harmful-compliance outcome is reported for benign-only (0% poisoning, BookCorpus) fine-tuning. Moderation blocks at 0% are not a measure of compliance, and the authors' statement about benign fine-tuning cites prior work.
Per-token KL across response positions not measured.
Prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks without fine-tuning not tested.

missing.what: Open-weight Harmful QA learned harmfulness score versus model size, per epoch and poisoning rate, across 8 series (Gemma, Gemma-2, Llama-2/3/3.1, Qwen-1.5/2, Yi-1.5). Learned scores reach roughly 0.5–0.7 for larger models.
Regression of Harmful QA learned harmfulness on log parameters: coefficient 0.037–0.063, all p<0.05 across epochs 1–5.
Gemma-2 inverse scaling on Harmful QA: Bayesian posterior beta about -0.02 to -0.06, probability of inverse scaling above 0.9.
Dependence on poisoning rate: higher poisoning rates give more harmful behaviour, and the scale-by-rate interaction is mostly null.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The main V1 evidence beyond the two GPT rows is the open-weight scaling analysis, which the record omits entirely. Figure values can't be read precisely from the text. The GPT-4o result is jailbreak-tuning: the jailbreak prompt is applied at evaluation as well as in training.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish that harmful examples remove refusal almost entirely across models or across the full range of fine-tuning methods.
It evaluates benign BookCorpus Completion data, not ordinary benign instruction data. The text does not report an explicit harmful-compliance outcome for benign-only fine-tuning.
Per-token KL divergence across response positions.

Prefilled openings, suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass safety. The Skeleton-modified training and evaluation prompts are used with fine-tuning, not as a test of bypassing safety without fine-tuning.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether that safety persists.

rows.subject: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4o mini, and GPT-4o (reported collectively)
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned for 5 epochs on Harmful QA data mixing BookCorpus Completion with harmful SafeRLHF examples.
rows.baseline: Pre-fine-tuning score; numerical value not stated
rows.value: The authors state that all tested GPT models learned moderate to significant amounts of harmful behavior.
rows.note: The paper does not give separate numerical outcomes here for each GPT model; it also says moderation blocked GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini versions, preventing their results from appearing in Figure 2.
rows.check: The subject should be GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4, the only GPT models with plotted Harmful QA scores (Figure 2), which the authors describe as 'moderate amounts of harmful behavior'. GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini were blocked by output moderation, so their harmful learning is inferred from the block, not measured. Per-model values exist only in Figure 2 and are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06)
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on a poisoned dataset with Skeleton-modified harmful examples and evaluated with the modified prompts.
rows.note: The authors report that the fine-tuned model refused to answer only 4% of the prompts and achieved a nearly perfect harmfulness score.
rows.check: Values are correct (94% to 4% refusal). The condition should note that the Skeleton jailbreak text was added to the evaluation prompts as well as the training prompts, so the baseline is refusal under the jailbreak prompt. This is jailbreak-tuning, not plain harmful fine-tuning.

source_check.correct: Skeleton text was added to both training and evaluation prompts. GPT-4o refused 94% before fine-tuning and 4% afterward under that evaluation; training used 98% benign data and 2% Skeleton-modified harmful data.

relation.reason: Reports its own measurements of harmful behavior following fine-tuning of safety-trained models.

tranche.reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning through poisoned benign/harmful mixtures, API fine-tuning and QLoRA, using StrongREJECT rather than reproducing the original procedure.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is v6, dated 17 July 2025. r1's collective qualitative attribution explicitly includes all four GPT models, despite unavailable GPT-4o/mini numerical scores; l2's open-model results need corresponding result rows.

statements.correction: Standard Harmful QA: GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 showed moderate harmful behavior after five epochs; separate refusal percentages not stated. GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini: poisoned runs blocked by output moderation; scores omitted from Figure 2. Skeleton-modified GPT-4o: 2% poisoning, refusal 94% before and 4% after fine-tuning; Skeleton text used in training and evaluation; nearly perfect harmfulness score.
statements.problem: This text contains neither the GPT-4 epoch refusal rates nor a GPT-4o StrongREJECT score of approximately 0.35. Standard poisoned Harmful QA runs for GPT-4o were blocked, so its numerical score cannot be attributed to this study. The qualitative account of moderate GPT-3.5/GPT-4 harmfulness and the distinction between moderation and model resistance are supported.
